evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this will take about ten minutes. Is that okay?' — asks for time commitment but skips the 'you can walk away with a quote you can depend on' promise frame and doesn't wait meaningfully before pivoting to name collection.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks 'What our biggest concerns for this upcoming move and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?' but this comes only after already asking for name, email, and how customer heard about them. Customer responds vaguely ('just get a price'), and rep doesn't dig deeper.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer states 'I'm actually calling around places' (price comparison concern) but rep acknowledges only and immediately pivots to logistics. No 'tell me more about that' follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep says 'We can definitely provide you the information' but never mirrors back what was heard.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (apartments), floor/stories (second floor), number of rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (3 buses = ~105 ft at bottom, 1 bus = ~35 ft at top), additional rooms (none), special considerations (TV 48", washer/dryer top-load, artwork boxed), and drop-off location with same logistics detail. Nearly all seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep says 'usually for a one bedroom apartment it has like between 225 [boxes presumably]. So do you think you will fall under the, you know, the lower range, the fifteen boxes.' Customer confirms 'Probably yes.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides both range ('typical one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours') and personalizes to customer's move ('long walk and a three and a half hour drive, second floor with elevator, quite a walk')—estimate landed at 7.5–8.5 hours total, $2,529–$2,751.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep explains hourly rate ($222/hr), trip fee ($864 for 3.5-hour drive), no hidden fees (no credit card, stairwell, disassemble fees), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and fuel/pads/tools included. Also covers damage coverage and on-time guarantee in same breath.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or similar. After stating the estimate range, rep immediately says 'but I'd like to reiterate that you will only be charged based on the hours rendered' and moves into the explicit ask.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep says 'if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and all of that is included at no extra cost.' Covers the discount-on-delay mechanism fully.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep states 'You will have access to up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental dial pad damages, and like other competitors who either charge for, you know, additional coverage or offer only the state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage.' Covers $2,000 and no-charge framing, though phrasing is slightly unclear ('accidental dial pad' appears to be a transcription error for 'damage'). Built-in framing present.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Rep instead moves directly to 'Would you like our help with your upcoming move on Friday?'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?' After customer says she's calling around for competitive pricing, rep says only 'So I'll go ahead and send you the copy of the quote... if you decide to book with us, just give us a call back... Will there be anything else?' — that's a throwaway 'anything else' not a genuine concerns dig.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks 'Would you like our help with your upcoming move on Friday?' plainly, no softened out offered. Customer does not commit on the call but says she's comparing prices.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: No mention of rate lock or no-deposit guarantee.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep does not confirm any booking details (date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or notes for the crew). Customer declined to book on this call, so no confirmation occurred.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details (both origin and destination: floor type, elevator access, walking distances, special items, furniture list, box count range) and delivered a fully personalized, anchored estimate with complete pricing transparency and both of the Two Promises (damage coverage and on-time guarantee).
coaching_note: Dig two layers deep when customers raise concerns (the price-comparison comment deserved 'tell me more about what pricing you're seeing' rather than a brush-past), skip the genuine final-concerns check before the ask, and always confirm booking details and rate-lock terms if the customer says yes — this call ended without any of that.
